Le novità saranno rivolte a offrire esperienze più fluide e integrate, con un focus sulla qualità del design, sulla durata della batteria e sulla connessione tra dispositivi. L’aggiornamento sarà pensato per rispondere alle esigenze di chi utilizza l’iPad per lavoro, studio e hobby. Si prevede una nuova generazione di modelli, con schermi più grandi e più sensibili, e una migliore gestione delle funzionalità di produzione e di consumo di energia. L’evoluzione dei software sarà anche un punto centrale, con integrazioni più profonde tra iPad e iPhone, oltre a nuove app e servizi. L’approccio sarà quello di rendere l’iPad ancora più versatile, sia come strumento di produttività che come piattaforma per la creatività. I partecipanti potranno gustare in diretta le presentazioni, mentre i tecnici e gli appassionati seguiranno con attenzione i dettagli tecnici e le caratteristiche innovative. La stampa e il pubblico attendono con interesse il lancio di nuovi prodotti che potrebbero riformulare il modo in cui si utilizza il tablet nel quotidiano.

L’intrattabile figura dell’infiltratore si colloca all’intersezione tra strategia, segretezza e rischio, rappresentando un agente specializzato nel raggiungimento di obiettivi sensibili all’interno di strutture o gruppi nemici, senza essere riconosciuto né riconosciuto come tale. L’infiltratore non opera per semplice presenza, ma attraverso un’adattabilità totale al contesto, imparando i modi di pensiero, le abitudini, i rituali e i linguaggi di chi lo circonda. La sua efficacia deriva da una profonda capacità di osservazione, di ascolto e di interpretazione di segnali sottostanti. Non si tratta di un semplice ostaggio della realtà, ma di un soggetto in costante trasformazione, che si dissolve in un ambiente per poi riemergere come elemento di influenza. Gli strumenti di lavoro sono molteplici: dal linguaggio alla fisica del movimento, dal corpo al silenzio. L’infiltrazione non è un atto di violenza, ma un gioco di posizione, un’arte della messa in scena di una presenza non riconoscibile. La sua esistenza è in sé una forma di dissoluzione, una sorta di metamorfosi volontaria. L’infiltratore si moltiplica nell’implicito, opera nel silenzio e nella complessità delle relazioni umane. La sua fine non è sempre nota, e spesso la sua verità rimane nascosta, come un segreto che non ha bisogsno di essere rivelato.

Il Small Computer System Interface, o SCSI, è un protocollo di comunicazione standardizzato sviluppato negli anni '80 per consentire la connessione tra periferiche di elaborazione e sistemi di elaborazione. Sviluppato originariamente da IBM, il SCSI permette di collegare dispositivi come dischi rigidi, unità di memoria, stampanti e schede grafiche a un computer attraverso una interfaccia elettrica e un protocollo di scambio dati. L'interfaccia, basata su un bus seriale, consente una velocità di trasmissione superiore rispetto ai protocolli precedenti, grazie a un'architettura semplice e scalabile. Il sistema utilizza un bus a più canali, con la possibilità di collegare fino a otto dispositivi in serie, ognuno identificato da un indirizzo univoco. Il protocollo è stato progressivamente evoluto con versioni successive come SCSI-2, SCSI-3 e SCSI-4, che hanno migliorato la velocità e la capacità di gestione dei dati. Il SCSI è stato ampiamente utilizzato nei sistemi personali e nei server negli anni '90, specialmente nei computer di alto livello e nei sistemi multi-dispositivo. Negli anni successivi, l'adozione ha diminuito in favore di protocolli come SATA e NVMe, tuttavia il SCSI continua a essere presente in alcuni settori specializzati, come l'industria della produzione di hardware o in applicazioni di archiviazione crittografata.

Marcos Camarda è un compositore e musicista italiano, nato a Roma nel 1967, noto per la sua attività nel campo della musica contemporanea e per la sua capacità di integrare elementi tradizionali del linguaggio musicale con approcci innovativi. Attivo sin dagli anni '80, Camarda ha sviluppato un'opera sonora che si muove tra il jazz, la musica classica e le forme espressive del postmodernismo. Ha collaborato con numerosi artisti e ensemble, sia in Italia che all'estero, contribuendo a progetti di ricerca e produzione musicale di rilevanza culturale. La sua opera si caratterizza per una forte sensibilità estetica, una chiara consapevolezza del contesto culturale e una capacità di scansionare il rapporto tra struttura sonora e espressione emotiva. Ha realizzato diversi progetti teatrali e sonori in cui la musica assume un ruolo narrativo e visivo, spaziando da spettacoli di piccolo formato a performance in contesti di elevata complessità. La sua ricerca artistica si colloca all'intersezione tra la musica come espressione individuale e come media sociale, esprimendo un'attenzione profonda alla forma, al tempo e alla comunicazione. Tra i suoi lavori più significativi, si ricordano opere per orchestra, per gruppi di strumenti e per performance in cui la musica si fonde con elementi di scrittura e scenografia. Camarda è riconosciuto come figura chiave nel panorama della musica contemporanea italiana, dove il suo lavoro si pone come ponte tra tradizione e innovazione.

Quelli che il calcio è un fenomeno culturale e sociale che ha radici profonde nell'esperienza collettiva delle comunità, sviluppandosi attraverso generazioni di giocatori, tifosi e organizzazioni sportive. Nasce come disciplina legata all'organizzazione di partite, alla regola del campo, al rapporto tra squadre e territori. Il calcio, nella sua forma più diffusa, si caratterizza per una semplicità di regole e una complessità emotiva che coinvolge migliaia di persone in ogni momento di gioco. Ogni partita diventa un evento, un momento di tensione, di speranza e di riconoscimento collettivo. Il gioco si ripete, si trasforma, si adatta agli spazi urbani e rurali, ai contesti politici e sociali. Il messaggio principale del calcio, come quello che il calcio, è la narrazione del sogno: quello di una squadra che vince, di un attaccante che batte l'arco, di un tifoso che si alza per un'azione di squadra. È una storia di imprevedibilità, di eroismo e di comunità, raccontata attraverso un linguaggio semplice ma profondo, attraverso gesti, urla, gesti di saluto, di appello, di solidarietà. Il calcio non si limita a un’attività fisica, è un modo di vivere, di credere, di essere uniti in un'immensa esperienza di appartenenza.

Le uova si conservano in frigorifero nei supermercati degli Stati Uniti, mentre in molti negozi europei non lo si fa. Questa differenza si spiega con il modo in cui le galline vengono allevate e con la presenza di una malattia diffusa nell’apparato digerente. Negli Stati Uniti, le galline vengono spesso allevate in ambienti industriali, dove le uova vengono raccolte rapidamente e conservate in condizioni di refrigerazione per prevenire l’alterazione. In Europa, al contrario, molte galline vivono in sistemi più naturali, in ambienti aperti e senza intubazioni, e le uova vengono raccolte in modo manuale, spesso direttamente sulle zampe. In queste condizioni, la malattia intestinale, nota come cistite o malattia dell’apparato digerente, si diffonde più facilmente. Le uova raccolte in questi ambienti non vengono refrigerate perché la loro superficie, più libera da contaminazioni, è meno soggetta a deteriorazione. Tuttavia, la conservazione in frigorifero aiuta a rallentare il processo di crescita microbica, soprattutto in caso di contaminazione. Per questo, la scelta di conservare o no le uova in frigo dipende non solo dalla cultura del produttore, ma anche dalla salute fisica delle galline e dalla presenza di patologie intestinali diffuse.

Pomigliano, nei giorni del referendum, non parlò mai. Non c’era nessuno a parlare per le strade, per i palazzi, per i balconi. Non c’era un sindaco che si alzasse, non c’era un gruppo che si riunisse, nessun avviso, nessuna voce che si diffondesse. Il silenzio non era semplice, era pesante. I cittadini camminavano, guardavano il cielo, ascoltavano le radio, ma non si sentivano ascoltati. Le strade erano vuote, i mercati chiusi, le scuole inattive. L’ansia si diffondeva, ma non si trasformava in azione. C’erano persone che si chiedevano cosa si stesse facendo, perché nessuno spiegava. I gruppi che si erano formati si dissolveno come nebbia. C’era un’impressione di abbandono, come se il tempo fosse bloccato. Le discussioni si fermavano al primo punto. Nessuno si faceva sentire, nessuno si pronunciava. Il voto era un fatto, ma il dibattito? Non c’era. Solo la routine, la vita quotidiana, come se nulla fosse cambiato. Eppure, quel giorno, c’era stato qualcosa di profondo, di invisibile, che si rifiutava di essere visto. Il popolo non si è sentito rappresentato. Il silenzio ha vinto. E nel silenzio, si è persa la possibilità di dire qualcosa di vero.

Hai riaperto gli occhi e il sole ancora non si è mosso. Il frigo ha ancora il suono del ghiaccio, il divano è ancora pieno di coperte. La finestra, aperta per un attimo, ha lasciato entrare un’aria che non si ricordava. Hai letto il giornale e l’hai lasciato su un tavolo che non è più tuo. L’acqua del rubinetto ha ancora quel sapore di estate, ma non c’è più nessuno che ne parla.  

Hai fatto scorrere le notizie come se fossero foglie che volano via. Il tempo si è fermato in un punto di mezzo, tra il saluto e la partenza. I numeri di ieri sono ancora sullo schermo, ma nessuno li ha guardati. La piazza vuota ha ricominciato a essere vuota, come se il mondo avesse deciso di non parlare.  

Hai visto un uomo che camminava con l’aria di chi non ha più bisogno di un posto dove stare. Il bar è aperto, ma nessuno ci entra. Il telefono ha ancora messo su un suono, ma non ha più risposto.  

Ti sei chiesto cosa fosse successo prima di oggi, prima che tu tornassi. E poi hai capito: era solo una domanda che non aveva bisogno di risposta.

Tião Neto, nato nel 1935 a Recife, in Brasile, è stato un musicista, cantante e compositore di origine popolare, noto soprattutto per aver incarnato con forza e autenticità la cultura musicale del Nordeste brasiliano. Appartenente alla scuola della musica popolare tradizionale, ha sviluppato un stile unico, che mescola elementi di folklorismo, di ritmo acustico e di narrazione orale, trasformando la musica in un mezzo di espressione sociale e culturale. Il suo lavoro ha avuto un'influenza profonda sulla musica popolare brasiliana, in particolare nel campo della canzone popolare e del ritmo "samba de roda". Attraverso canzoni che spesso trattano temi di vita quotidiana, di emozioni umane e di identità regionale, Tião Neto ha offerto una voce autentica e profonda, che ha unito generazioni e ha contribuito a riconoscere il valore della cultura popolare come parte integrante dell'eredità artistica del Brasile. La sua musica, spesso realizzata con strumenti semplici e con un forte uso della voce, è stata un ponte tra il passato e il presente, tra la tradizione e l'innovazione. Oltre alla sua attività musicale, Tião Neto ha promosso la diffusione della cultura del Nordeste, favorendo la trasmissione di conoscenze e storie attraverso il suono. La sua carriera è stata caratterizzata da un'attenzione costante alla genuinità artistica e alla preservazione delle radici culturali.

Pietro di Porto è un nome che emerge nel panorama culturale e storico della regione del sud Italia, in particolare nel territorio del mezzogiorno, dove le tradizioni locali e le figure di intellettuale hanno sempre mantenuto un ruolo centrale. Nato a Porto, comune del territorio pugliese, Pietro di Porto si inserisce nel contesto di una serie di pensatori che hanno cercato di riunire l’eredità del pensiero classico con le esigenze del presente. Non è un nome noto in ambito accademico internazionale, ma nel suo territorio di origine ha raggiunto una certa visibilità attraverso opere scritte su storia locale, letteratura e formazione dei giovani. Le sue opere, scritte in un linguaggio diretto e profondo, riflettono un’attenzione particolare per le radici culturali della provincia, il ruolo del paesaggio nel formare l’identità e la necessità di un’educazione che non si limiti al sapere teorico. Ha collaborato con istituzioni locali per promuovere la scuola e il patrimonio storico. Non ha mai pubblicato opere a carattere internazionale, ma il suo impatto si è manifestato in un’ampia rete di insegnanti e studenti che hanno tratto ispirazione dalle sue riflessioni. La sua figura è quindi più un esempio di impegno civile che di produzione accademica, incarnando un’idea di conoscenza legata alla comunità e alla terra.

Il Cane di Giava, noto anche come *Canis javanicus*, è una razza canina originaria delle isole del Mar Cinese e in particolare dell'isola di Giava, situata nell'arcipelago indonesiano. Questa specie, appartenente alla famiglia dei cani, si distingue per un corpo robusto, un pelo lungo e spesso, di colore marrone o grigio, e per un'agilità notevole, adatta a movimenti rapidi su terreni accidentati. I cani di Giava sono stati tradizionalmente utilizzati come animali da compagnia, ma anche come cani di caccia, soprattutto per la caccia alle specie di uccelli e roditori che popolano le foreste locali. La loro resistenza all'ambiente tropicale e la capacità di adattarsi a condizioni climatiche estreme hanno contribuito alla loro diffusione in diverse zone dell'Asia orientale. Studi etnografici indicano che questi cani sono stati per lungo tempo parte integrante delle comunità rurali, dove svolgevano ruoli pratici e simbolici. Attualmente, a causa della perdita di habitat e della frammentazione del territorio, la popolazione del Cane di Giava è in rapida diminuzione, classificandolo come specie a rischio di estinzione. L'UNESCO e organismi internazionali hanno avviato campagne di conservazione per preservare questa razza, promuovendo la ricerca scientifica e il riconoscimento della sua importanza bioculturale.

Federico Ashton è un nome che, nel panorama culturale e artistico contemporaneo, non compare come figura centrale né documentata in fonti autorevole. Non si individua in archivi storici, nel catalogo di opere, né nei riferimenti accademici di discipline letterarie o artistiche. La sua presenza, se mai si manifesta, è diffusa in ambienti locali, in contesti di piccola circolazione, o in progetti di natura dilettantistica, dove si può osservare un uso di nomi falsi o ricreati per fini di espressione individuale o di sperimentazione linguistica. Nelle fonti pubbliche non emergono dati sulle sue attività, sulla formazione, sull'esperienza professionale o sulle opere realizzate. L'identità di Federico Ashton rimane in tal modo incerta, talvolta oggetto di interpretazione, altre volte di aneddoti privati o di invenzioni narrative. Si tratta di un nome che appare in certi contesti come espressione di un'idea più ampia: quella di un soggetto in via di costruzione, di un'immagine che si forma attraverso l'uso del nome, piuttosto che attraverso la presenza reale. È un esempio di come il nome possa diventare più significativo non per la sua provenienza, ma per il suo potere simbolico, per la sua capacità di evocare un vuoto o un'incertezza che, nel linguaggio, diventa spazio per nuove espressioni.

Luca si sveglia sempre prima dell’alba, con le mani strette attorno al cuscino, perché ogni tocco dell’acqua, anche quello del piumino, gli scuote la pelle. Il corpo gli risponde con un’orticaria improvvisa, come un urlo silenzioso. Non si lava mai, non si asciuga mai. La sua casa è un'isola di cotone, di tessuti morbidi, di spazio vuoto. Il dì del bagno è una storia che non si racconta, perché l’acqua è l’ultima cosa che può toccare. Maria, in un paese del sud, ha imparato a vivere senza muro, senza vasca, senza doccia. I suoi vestiti sono sempre asciutti, anche dopo un giorno di sole. La luce del giorno entra solo attraverso finestre che non si aprono mai. Luca ha paura del sole, perché la luce calda fa aumentare il prurito. Non ha mai visto un mare, perché il primo contatto con l’acqua gli ha fatto male. Lui e altri 32, nel mondo, vivono in silenzio, in una forma di vita che non è più comune. Non si bagnano, non si rinfrescano, non si sciolgono. Eppure, ogni giorno, l’acqua passa, e loro rimangono. Un mondo senza acqua, eppure, un cuore che batte.

Booknotes was an American television series broadcast on the C-SPAN network from 1989 to 2004. Hosted by Brian Lamb, each episode presented a one-hour conversation with the author of a recently published nonfiction book. Lamb asked writers about their research, their influences and the choices they made while writing. Its unhurried format allowed authors to discuss their work at length, and the archive remains useful to researchers.

Police investigating the rape of an elderly nun in the Indian state of West Bengal have made their first arrests, more than 12 days after the crime was committed. The delay drew criticism from religious leaders and community groups, who said the case needed a faster response. Officials have since asked residents for any information that could help the inquiry, which is continuing.

The Leavenworth Riverfront Community Center is a public facility in Leavenworth, Washington, a small town in the Cascade Mountains known for its alpine-style architecture. It sits near the Wenatchee River and hosts meetings, classes and community events for residents and visitors. Published information about its construction and operating history is limited, so details such as opening dates should be confirmed with the city.

The Peruvian army says it has rescued 39 people from a farm where members of the Shining Path rebel group had held them in conditions of forced labour. Soldiers carried out the operation in a remote rural area. Officials did not immediately say how long the workers had been held. Authorities have opened an investigation into the case and have begun arranging medical checks and support for those rescued.

Angelina Jolie Pitt, the special envoy of the United Nations refugee agency, has warned that the international system for helping refugees is breaking down. Funding shortfalls, rising numbers of displaced people and reluctance among some governments to accept new arrivals have left aid agencies stretched, she said. Her comments come as countries debate how to share responsibility for refugees and as conditions in many camps have worsened.

Burkina Faso's interim president, Michel Kafando, has been freed and is in good health, the leaders of the new military junta said. Kafando had been detained after soldiers seized power in the capital, Ouagadougou, and the junta's statement offered reassurance about his condition after days of uncertainty. Regional mediators and foreign governments have urged the new leaders to restore civilian rule quickly.

Northern Ireland's outgoing chief electoral officer has said that the cost of holding the Assembly election in March is likely to reach about £5 million. The figure reflects staffing, printing and security arrangements at polling stations. Officials have also asked the government for clarity on funding before the vote is called. A final estimate is expected later in the year.

Sony Professional Solutions was a business unit of the Japanese electronics company Sony, responsible for equipment used in broadcasting, film production and other professional media work. Its product range included cameras, video recorders, monitors and editing systems sold to television stations, studios and production companies. The unit's name and organisational structure changed several times as Sony reorganised its electronics business, and its products have since been managed under other divisions.

Puerto Rico Highway 821 is a secondary road on the island of Puerto Rico, part of the numbered network that links towns and rural communities away from the main expressways. Routes of this kind usually carry lighter traffic than primary roads, and local residents rely on them daily. Its exact length and alignment are listed in the official road inventory kept by the Puerto Rico Highway and Transportation Authority.

A full military funeral has been held for a soldier who died in a helicopter crash in Afghanistan. Family members, fellow soldiers and senior officers attended the service, which followed the traditions of a military honour guard. Officials paid tribute to the soldier's service and offered condolences to the family. The cause of the crash is still under investigation.

Angola, one of Africa's largest oil producers, has asked the International Monetary Fund for financial assistance. The request comes as falling oil revenue has strained government finances and reduced the country's foreign currency reserves. Officials are expected to discuss the details of any programme with IMF staff in the coming weeks, and the outcome will depend on how far the government is willing to reform public spending.

A seven-bed dementia ward based in Yeovil, Somerset, is to close in July because of ongoing difficulties in recruiting specialist staff. The local health trust said the decision had not been taken lightly and that patients would be moved to other wards or units in the area. Relatives and staff have raised concerns about the impact on people living with dementia, who often find moves between wards distressing. The trust said it would keep looking for ways to provide specialist care locally.

Championship club Hull City have appointed Leonid Slutsky as their new head coach, the club has announced. Slutsky, who previously coached the Russian national team, takes charge of a squad that has been looking for a more consistent run of results. The appointment brings an experienced international coach to the club and ends a period of uncertainty over the managerial role. Slutsky is expected to meet players and begin preparations for the next match in the coming days.

The Diebold Professor of Comparative Philology is an academic chair in the study of related languages and their historical development, a discipline that compares texts and grammatical structures across languages to reconstruct how they changed over time. Endowed professorships of this kind are funded by a benefactor, and the holder is usually expected to teach and supervise research. The name honours the donors who established the post, and the details of its endowment are not widely documented in public sources.

The Tyne and Wear Metro, the light rail network serving Newcastle upon Tyne and surrounding areas in north-east England, is to receive a multi-million pound investment to modernise its infrastructure. Over the next year, work is expected to focus on upgrading stations, track and systems, with the aim of improving reliability and the passenger experience. Transport officials say the programme will minimise disruption where possible, though some temporary service changes are likely while the work takes place.

Administrative discretion is the power that legislation gives public officials to choose among possible courses of action when deciding a matter. Rather than applying a fixed rule to every case, an official weighs the circumstances and decides what response is appropriate, within the limits set by the statute that grants the power. Most legal systems require that it be used for proper purposes and in a reasonable way.

West Dunbartonshire Council has secured a grant of £500,000 to restore the historic Dumbarton Academy building, a move the council says will protect one of the town's most recognisable landmarks. The council has been working to find money for the building's repair, and the grant marks a significant step towards starting that work.

Council leaders said the restoration would safeguard the fabric of the building and open up new possibilities for its use by local groups and visitors. Local councillors welcomed the announcement, which they said reflected months of work by council officers. Details of the project, including its timetable and total cost, will be confirmed once the council has finalised its plans with the funders and its design team.

Dumbarton, a former burgh on the River Clyde, has a long history tied to shipbuilding and to the castle that stands on the volcanic rock above the town. Heritage groups have argued that restoring civic buildings can help support tourism and local pride. Because the building sits in a central part of the town, its condition is closely watched by residents.

Biswanath Mukherjee is a computer scientist best known for his research on optical networks, the high-capacity systems that carry data over fibre-optic cables. He is a professor in the Department of Computer Science at the University of California, Davis, where his work has covered wavelength-division multiplexing, network design and the survivability of networks after equipment failures. His research has been widely cited in the field, and his textbook on optical networking has been used in graduate courses at several universities.

His work is generally described as concerned with how large optical networks can be designed and operated efficiently as demand for bandwidth grows. Several of the ideas associated with his research have become standard material in the field, and students studying communications networks often encounter them in their first years of graduate study.

Biographical details beyond his academic career are less widely published, and readers seeking more personal information should consult institutional profiles or the professional societies to which he belongs.

Little has been published about Nicole Breault, and the public record of her life and work is correspondingly thin. Where information exists, it tends to come from local press coverage, professional directories and occasional mentions in institutional publications, rather than from a full biography or a sustained body of commentary. That is not unusual for someone whose activities have never drawn sustained attention in print.

Anyone trying to build a reliable account of her career should begin with primary records, such as official announcements, employer listings or the publications she is credited with, and should treat secondary summaries with caution. Because the available material is limited, the most accurate description that can be given is a cautious one. Readers who need specific dates, roles or achievements should verify each claim against a source they can examine directly. Where a claim cannot be checked, it is better to leave it out than to guess. A short, accurate entry is worth more than a long one built on guesswork.

Donald Trump's visit to Mexico on Wednesday came somewhat out of the blue, with the trip announced only a day before it took place. The Republican presidential candidate travelled to Mexico City to meet the country's president, Enrique Peña Nieto, in talks that focused on migration, trade and the security of the border. Officials on both sides described the meeting as a chance to discuss shared concerns, although the public statements that followed gave little detail of what was agreed. The visit drew immediate attention in both countries, not least because Trump had spent much of his campaign criticising Mexico over trade and immigration and calling for a wall along the southern border. Mexican commentators were divided over whether the trip signalled diplomatic engagement or a political risk for a president who had faced criticism for extending the invitation. Some analysts argued that the meeting offered the candidate a chance to appear presidential, while others questioned whether it would change his stance on the issues that had defined his campaign. The schedule was not publicly confirmed until shortly before the meeting, and the trip quickly became one of the main talking points of the campaign. Opponents seized on the timing and the content of the discussions, and supporters praised the decision to engage directly with the Mexican government.

Ian Chipchase is a person whose public profile is modest, and the reliable information about him is correspondingly limited. Most of what is available comes from short mentions in local or specialist publications, and there is no widely cited biography that sets out his life in detail.

The surname itself has a clear geographic association. Chipchase is most often found among families from northern England, particularly in Northumberland, where a castle of the same name stands in the countryside near the River North Tyne. The family name has been recorded in local documents for many generations, and it is shared by people in several professions.

Because the surname is common enough to appear in many unrelated records, any attempt to link a particular person with a given role or achievement needs to be checked against the original source. A careful reader should therefore separate what is documented about the surname from what can be confirmed about the individual, and should check the date, place and context of any record before accepting it as relevant.

Gethin Jenkins returns to captain Cardiff Blues for Thursday's Challenge Cup Pool Three match in Montpellier, the club has confirmed. The Wales prop, one of the most experienced forwards in the squad, will lead the team in a fixture that could prove decisive for the side's hopes of reaching the knockout stages.

His return gives the coaching staff an experienced figure in the front row at a time when several players are being rotated. Jenkins's leadership is likely to matter in a match where the pack can decide the tempo. Cardiff Blues have been hoping to build momentum after an uneven run in the competition, and a win in southern France would strengthen their position in the pool.

Montpellier are a demanding opponent on their home ground, and the Welsh side will need discipline at the scrum and at the breakdown to contain the home team's forwards. Coaches are expected to name the full matchday squad later in the week. The match is expected to draw a sizeable crowd, and the result will be watched closely by fans in Wales, who have followed the club's European campaign with growing interest.

Highway 818 in Puerto Rico is a secondary route, one of the numbered roads that carry traffic between towns and rural areas beyond the main expressway system. Like many roads of its class, it is narrower in places than the island's primary highways and follows the contours of the land, which changes from flat coastal plain to rolling hills further inland.

Secondary highways on the island serve a mix of purposes. They carry residents to schools, clinics and markets, connect farms to larger roads and provide alternatives when a primary route is congested or closed. Maintenance and repair are the responsibility of the territorial transport authority, which sets priorities across the network according to traffic levels, safety records and funding. Anyone travelling the route for the first time should also check for recent closures or works, which are common on secondary roads after heavy rain.

Because details such as the precise length, sections and junctions of individual routes change over time, the most reliable source for current information is the official road inventory published by the territorial government. Local maps and transport planning documents can also help clarify how the route fits into the wider network.

Newport County have agreed a 10-year lease with Newport Rugby to play their home games at Rodney Parade, the club has announced. The arrangement secures the football club's base for the long term and brings an end to months of uncertainty over where the team would play in the coming seasons.

Rodney Parade has been home to Newport's rugby side for many years, and the ground is closely associated with the city's sporting heritage. Under the new agreement, both clubs will continue to use the stadium, and the football club will take on responsibility for organising its own matchday operations. Officials from both organisations said the deal reflected a shared commitment to keeping the venue in active use.

For supporters, the lease offers stability after a period in which the future of the club's home fixtures had been the subject of discussion. Fans can now plan for the longer term, and the club said it would look at ways to improve facilities for spectators during the coming season.

The lease terms are expected to be finalised in the coming weeks, after which the club will confirm its fixture arrangements with the league. Supporters have been encouraged to renew their season tickets while the arrangements are confirmed.

Three shops in Pontypridd that were bought by the Welsh Government have been sold on for about £980,000 less than the purchase price. The properties were acquired as part of efforts to support the regeneration of the town centre, so the loss is likely to prompt questions about how public money was spent on the project. The original purchase price and the terms of the sale are expected to face further scrutiny.

Property values in smaller town centres have been under pressure for some years, and buildings that need significant repair can be hard to sell at a profit. Officials will be expected to explain the reasons for the difference between the two prices, including the condition of the buildings and the state of the market when the sale was agreed.

Pontypridd, a town in the Rhondda Cynon Taf area of south Wales, has been the focus of several regeneration schemes over the past decade. Local traders often say that empty units and low footfall remain the main obstacles to recovery, and many welcome any investment that could bring new businesses to the centre.

Whether the sale will affect future plans for the area is not yet clear. The details of any review or audit will determine how far the matter is pursued, and residents will be watching closely to see whether lessons are learned.

HMRC has rejected criticism from Andrew Tyrie, chairman of the Treasury select committee, over the way it responded to the exploitation of tax breaks for the film industry. The committee had argued that the tax authority should have acted more quickly and more decisively once it became aware that schemes were being used to claim relief in ways Parliament did not intend.

HMRC said it had taken the issue seriously and had worked to tighten the rules and close loopholes as they were identified. Officials argued that the department had responded in proportion to the risks, and that some of the arrangements under scrutiny were lawful at the time they were used.

The dispute reflects a wider debate about how far tax authorities should intervene in areas where the law is complex and where schemes can be designed to take advantage of gaps in legislation. Committee members have generally argued for firmer action, while officials have emphasised the need to protect taxpayers from unfair or retrospective changes.

The row is likely to continue as the committee examines the department's response and considers whether further reforms are needed to prevent similar problems in the future.

The mother of a seven-year-old girl who battled cancer is facing prosecution for failing to send her daughter to school. The case has drawn sympathy from parents and campaigners, who say that families dealing with serious illness need flexibility and support rather than court action.

According to the family's account, the girl's health made regular attendance very difficult during and after treatment, and her mother had been trying to balance the child's medical needs with the demands of education. Local education authorities generally have a legal duty to ensure that children of compulsory school age attend school, and officers say they are required to follow a set process before any prosecution begins.

Charities that work with families affected by childhood cancer say that many pupils face long periods away from the classroom and that schools often need to adapt. They have called for clearer guidance so that pupils who are unwell can return gradually and receive help with their lessons without families being penalised.

The case is expected to be heard in the coming weeks, and the outcome may influence how other councils handle attendance for children with serious medical conditions.

Kamil is a common given name in Poland, and Wojtkowski is a Polish surname derived from a personal name with the suffix typical of many Polish family names. Because both parts of the name are widely used, a search for Kamil Wojtkowski returns records for several different people in different fields, and it is not possible to say from the name alone which of them is meant.

Documented biographical material on any specific individual with this name is sparse in English-language sources. Polish-language directories, professional registers and local press are more likely to contain relevant entries, though these also need to be checked for consistency, since people with the same name are easily confused in online listings. Cross-checking two independent sources is a sensible minimum.

Readers who need to identify a particular Kamil Wojtkowski should look for an identifying detail, such as a profession, city of residence or date of birth, and match it against an original source. Without that, any single biography would risk combining the records of different people, which is a common error in reference works built from search results. A short entry that states only what can be confirmed is more useful than a longer one built on assumption.

Kitcharao is a municipality in the province of Agusan del Norte, in the Caraga region of the Philippines. Like many towns in northeastern Mindanao, it has an economy rooted in agriculture, and farming and the processing of crops form an important part of local livelihoods. The municipality is divided into barangays, the smallest administrative units in the country, and its town centre serves as the seat of local government.

The landscape combines lowland farmland with hills and forest further inland, and the climate is tropical, with rainfall that is heavy for much of the year. Such conditions support the cultivation of rice, coconut and other crops, though farmers in the region have faced challenges from typhoons and flooding in recent years.

Local government in Kitcharao is organised around an elected mayor and municipal council, which are responsible for services such as health, roads, markets and basic education. Schools and health facilities in the municipality are linked to provincial and national programmes.

Population and census figures for the municipality change between counts and are updated regularly, so they should be checked against the most recent national statistics. Visitors interested in local history or culture can find more information from the provincial government or the municipal office.

Several judges and lawyers named David Simmons have worked in common-law jurisdictions, and public information about any one of them can be hard to separate from the others. Judicial appointments are usually recorded in official gazettes, court announcements and law society publications, which are the most reliable places to confirm when a person was appointed and to which court.

Judges of this kind typically hear cases in a trial court or an appellate court, and their careers often include earlier work as a barrister, solicitor or prosecutor. Biographical summaries prepared for courts and professional bodies usually list qualifications, dates of appointment and any notable decisions, though the depth of detail varies widely from one jurisdiction to another.

Where a published biography of a judge exists, it is often based on the court's own notices or on press coverage of significant rulings. Anyone writing about a specific David Simmons should identify the court and the period of service first, because without those details it is easy to attribute a decision or appointment to the wrong person.

Because the given name and surname are both common, this entry does not assign a single career to the name. Readers who need an account of a particular judge should consult the official court records for the relevant jurisdiction.

Mellieħa Redoubt is a small fortification at Mellieħa, a town on the northern coast of Malta, built as part of the island's defences against naval attack. Coastal works of this kind were common across the Maltese islands, which occupied a strategic position in the central Mediterranean and were fortified by successive rulers over many centuries.

A redoubt is a defensive position, usually a compact earthwork or stone structure designed to hold a small garrison and to cover approaches with fire. Redoubts on Malta were often placed on high ground or near landing beaches, where they could observe shipping and support larger fortifications nearby.

Over time, many of these works lost their original military role as weapons and tactics changed. Some were converted to other uses, while others were left to deteriorate or were incorporated into later developments. The conservation of the surviving structures has become an important concern for heritage bodies, which seek to balance public access with the protection of the fabric.

Visitors interested in the site can usually learn more from Maltese heritage authorities, local museums and guidebooks about the island's military architecture, which is one of its most distinctive features.

A surfer who was rescued after 32 hours adrift at sea has told his family that he had come to terms with the possibility that he would not survive. The man, who was pulled from the water after a long search, said he had tried to stay calm and conserve his energy while waiting for help to arrive.

Rescuers were alerted when his absence was reported, and a search was launched across a wide area of open water. Crews worked through the night and into the following day, covering the stretch of coast where he was last seen.

Friends and relatives described the moment of his rescue as overwhelming, and his family has thanked the crews for their persistence. Medical staff assessed him after he was brought ashore, and he was reported to be in a stable condition while doctors continued to monitor his health.

Water safety organisations said the case showed the value of carrying a flotation device and of telling someone on shore where you plan to surf. Surfers are often encouraged to check tide and weather forecasts before heading out, particularly when conditions are changing.

Welsh football fans are preparing to travel to France in their thousands this month, after their national team qualified for the European Championships for the first time in 58 years. The trip has become one of the most eagerly anticipated events in the country's sporting calendar, and supporters' groups have been arranging coaches, flights and accommodation for weeks.

The qualification marks a turning point for a team that has spent decades as a regular outsider on the international stage. Wales had not reached a major finals since the 1958 World Cup, and the squad's success has been widely celebrated across the country. Many supporters say the team has given them a sense of pride that extends well beyond the football pitch.

Travel has been complicated by the number of people wanting to make the journey, and the Football Association of Wales has urged fans to plan carefully, to book accommodation early and to check local rules and transport arrangements in the host cities. Organisers said they expected large numbers of supporters to head to the tournament venues, and that they were working with police and local authorities to ensure a safe and orderly experience.

For many fans, the chance to watch their team at a major tournament is something they never expected to see in their lifetime. Some have spoken of parents and grandparents who followed earlier campaigns with less success, and they hope the squad will leave a lasting legacy for the next generation of players and supporters.

The team's preparations have been closely watched, with attention focused on the squad's fitness, its tactical options and the availability of key players. Coaches have said the group is determined to make the most of its opportunity, and that the experience of playing against established football nations will be valuable in the years ahead.

Businesses in the towns where Welsh supporters will gather are preparing for an influx of visitors, and several bars and hotels have reported strong advance bookings. Tourism officials in Wales have said the tournament could showcase the country to an international audience, although they caution that the benefits will depend on how well the travelling fans are welcomed and how smoothly the event is run.

Fans who cannot make the trip are following the build-up on television and online, and many local clubs are planning screenings and gatherings to share the experience. The enthusiasm has spread far beyond the usual football crowd, with families, schools and community groups all looking forward to the tournament.

Katrin Flikschuh is a philosopher whose work concentrates on political philosophy, the history of modern European thought and the moral philosophy of Immanuel Kant. She has held academic posts in Britain, where she has taught and supervised students in philosophy departments and contributed to the teaching of political theory. Her writing is known for close attention to the texts it discusses.

Her early scholarship examined Kant's account of freedom and law, and in particular the relation between individual autonomy and the authority of the state. Her interpretation of Kant's political writings emphasises that they are more than a theory of institutions, and that they contain a substantive account of how people can be bound by law without losing their standing as free agents. Specialists in Kantian scholarship have engaged with these arguments in articles and in monographs.

Her monograph Kant and Modern Political Philosophy, published by Cambridge University Press in 2000, is among the works most often cited in this area. The book explores how Kant's ideas shaped later debates about justice, rights and the legitimacy of political authority, and it places his theory within the tradition of contract and consent.

Flikschuh has also written on the concept of freedom more broadly. Her introduction to the subject, Freedom: A Philosophical Introduction, sets out the main accounts of freedom found in the history of philosophy and explains the disputes between them. The book is used in university courses and is often recommended to students approaching the topic for the first time.

Across her publications, Flikschuh has returned to questions about how the state should treat individuals who hold different views of the good life, and about the limits of what public institutions may require of citizens. Her work engages with both historical texts and contemporary debates, and it has contributed to renewed interest in the normative foundations of political liberalism.

Kant's political philosophy remains a central reference point for discussions of republicanism, cosmopolitan order and the rights of persons, and scholars working on these topics continue to test interpretations of the texts against contemporary problems. Work of this kind often concentrates on a small number of passages, such as the discussions of property, contract and the status of the citizen, which are read closely and compared with other accounts.

Readers seeking a fuller account of her career should consult her university profile and her list of publications, which provide dates and details not given here. Where a biographical claim cannot be confirmed from a reliable source, it is best treated with caution.

Idealization is the deliberate simplification or distortion of a system in a scientific model, undertaken so that the model can be understood, calculated or tested. In philosophy of science, the concept is central to discussions about how models relate to the world, because most models leave out features that real systems possess and sometimes add assumptions that are known to be false.

A classic example is the frictionless plane in classical mechanics. Students learn to analyse the motion of a block on an inclined plane without friction, and only later are they asked to add the effects of friction, air resistance and the irregular surfaces of real objects. The simplified case is not mistaken in the sense of being a mere error; it is a tool that isolates a particular causal relationship and makes its consequences tractable.

Philosophers have distinguished several kinds of idealization. Galilean idealization involves assumptions that are knowingly false but that are used to pick out the essential features of a phenomenon, with the expectation that additional factors can be introduced later. By contrast, what is sometimes called Aristotelian idealization involves abstracting from features of a system in order to study a kind of thing in its pure form, without assuming that the excluded features are absent in the world.

The distinction matters for questions about explanation and about the status of scientific laws. If a model depends on idealizing assumptions, it becomes important to ask whether the explanation it provides holds for real systems, and under what conditions it might fail. Some writers argue that idealized models can nonetheless explain real phenomena by revealing the core structure that underlies them, while others are more sceptical about whether such explanations can be trusted.

Another problem concerns the process of de-idealization, in which the simplifying assumptions of a model are gradually relaxed to produce more realistic predictions. Advocates argue that this procedure shows how idealized theories can be connected to the complex world, whereas critics point out that the process is rarely straightforward and may require ad hoc adjustments.

Idealization has also been studied in the social sciences and in economics, where models of rational agents or perfectly competitive markets rely heavily on assumptions that are known to be unrealistic. Debates there often focus on whether such models are useful for prediction, policy or understanding, and on how their assumptions can be justified. These questions connect to wider issues about the role of models in science, including how they represent, how they are validated and how their limits should be communicated.

Greatorex is the name of an electoral division, a geographic area used to elect a representative to a legislative body or local council. Electoral divisions are a common feature of systems of government in several countries, and the name of a division usually reflects the place or the historical area that the boundaries enclose.

Division boundaries are normally set by an independent boundary commission or an equivalent body, which takes account of population size, community ties and the convenience of voters. The aim is to produce divisions that are broadly equal in population, so that each representative speaks for a similar number of residents. In practice, boundaries are reviewed periodically, and changes in population can lead to the redrawing of divisions and to the renaming of some areas.

The information available about an individual division can vary widely. For some divisions, official records list the population, the electorate, the number of seats and the results of recent elections. For others, especially those that are small or that have been altered several times, the details can be harder to trace, and the historical record may be incomplete.

Electoral divisions of this kind typically contain a mix of residential, commercial and rural land, and their character depends on the economic and social make-up of the area. Some divisions are largely urban, others cover towns and surrounding countryside, and a few contain little more than a village and its farmland. Local services such as schools, health facilities and roads are usually the responsibility of other bodies, but the representative for the division often acts as a link between residents and those bodies.

When studying the history of a division, it is useful to consult the official boundary reports, the records of local councils and the results of past elections, which are often published by electoral authorities. Changes to the boundaries can make comparisons between periods difficult, so it is important to note the year in which each set of boundaries took effect. In many systems the commission must also publish its reasons, so that the public can judge whether the proposals are fair.

Voters and researchers alike benefit from clear information about who represents a division and how its boundaries are defined. Election results, candidate lists and turnout figures can reveal patterns of political support over time, and they can help to explain how local priorities have shifted. Where specific details about a particular division are required, the most reliable approach is to check the official electoral register and the published reports of the body responsible for drawing the boundaries.

Because a division's name can also be shared by other places or families, researchers should confirm which area is meant before drawing conclusions. A careful reference entry will therefore distinguish between the general features of electoral divisions and the particular facts about one division, and it will rely on primary sources for any figures it gives.

The Prince of Wales and the Duchess of Cornwall have met staff from Manchester Arena who were among the first people on the scene after last month's suicide bombing at the venue. The couple spent time talking with employees, volunteers and emergency responders, hearing accounts of the night when an explosion killed and injured concertgoers as they left the building.

The visit was part of a wider programme of engagements in the city, which has been seeking to recover from the attack and to support those affected. Royal visitors often spend time with frontline workers after major incidents, and the couple's meeting was intended to recognise the courage shown by staff who helped people in the minutes and hours that followed the blast.

Many of the arena's employees were working at the venue on the evening of the concert, and some were injured or traumatised by what they saw. Staff who were on duty that evening have spoken of the difficulty of returning to work, and some want to find ways of keeping alive the memory of those who died in the attack.

Manchester has been the focus of sustained public attention since the bombing, and the city's response has been marked by a strong sense of solidarity. Residents, businesses and community groups have organised vigils, fundraising events and charity appeals, and many have stressed the importance of supporting families who lost loved ones.

The visit also came at a time when the authorities were reviewing the response to the attack, including the security arrangements at large venues and the procedures used to evacuate crowds. Officials have said that lessons from the incident will be considered carefully, although the detailed findings of any inquiry are still to come.

For the staff who met the royal visitors, the occasion was a chance to speak about their experiences and to be acknowledged for their actions on the night. Those who attended said the conversations had been moving, and that the reminder of the public's gratitude was welcome as the city continued its recovery.

The couple's engagement comes as Manchester prepares to mark the anniversary of the attack in the months ahead, with memorial services planned and support services expected to remain in place for those still recovering from their injuries. Many people in the city hope the response to the tragedy will be remembered for the compassion shown by ordinary people as much as for the loss of life.

Several people have carried the name Cian Nugent, and the surname and given name are both found in Ireland and in other English-speaking countries. Because the combination is not unusual, reference material about a person with this name should be checked against a specific profession, location or date before it is relied on.

The given name Cian is an Irish name, generally glossed as meaning something like enduring or long-lasting, and it has been popular in Ireland for many decades. It is often spelt with a fada over the first vowel in Irish-language contexts, although the unaccented form is common in English. The name is used for men and boys, and it has become familiar to readers and listeners through sport, the arts and public life.

The surname Nugent has a long history in Ireland. It comes from a Norman family that settled in the country after the Anglo-Norman invasion of the twelfth century, and branches of the family became prominent in the landed gentry, in the army and in public office. Several Irish and British families with the name trace their descent to this origin, though the surname has also spread through migration to other parts of the world.

Because the name is shared by several people, it is worth separating what is known about the surname from what can be confirmed about any individual who bears it. Records such as birth registers, electoral rolls, professional directories and published sporting or cultural records can help establish which person is being discussed. Press coverage can be useful too, but articles should be checked to make sure they refer to the right person.

Anyone writing a biography for a specific Cian Nugent should begin with a fixed point of identification, such as the field in which he worked or the place where he lived, and build the account from primary sources. Where that information is missing, a general description of the name is the safest form of reference. Errors in this area often occur when details from unrelated people are merged into a single entry, and a careful writer will avoid that by noting the uncertainty openly.

The name also illustrates how Irish personal names are used internationally. Families in Ireland, Britain, North America and Australia have given the name to children, and the surname continues to appear in records from many countries. This spread means that the same name can attach to people with very different backgrounds and careers.

machine.topic: List of mayors of Tukwila, Washington
machine.text:
Tukwila is a city in King County, Washington, located just south of Seattle and adjacent to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. It was incorporated more than a century ago and has grown into a mixed community of residential neighbourhoods, industrial areas and commercial districts, with a population that has changed considerably since the middle of the twentieth century.

Like many cities in Washington, Tukwila uses a mayor-council form of government, in which the mayor serves as the chief executive and is responsible for the day-to-day administration of city departments. The city council serves as the legislative body, sets policy, approves the budget and considers ordinances. The mayor and council members are elected in local elections, and their terms are set out in the city's charter and in state law.

A list of the city's mayors provides a record of local leadership over more than a century. Such lists are usually compiled from municipal minutes, election records, state archives and local histories, and they are most useful when they include the dates of each term, the manner in which the mayor came to office and any change in the form of government. Because the early records of small cities can be incomplete, some dates may be approximate or may differ between sources.

Changes in the mayor's office often reflected broader developments in the area, including the expansion of the airport, the growth of the regional highway network and shifts in the local economy. Tukwila's location at the junction of major roads and rail lines meant that its civic affairs were closely tied to regional planning decisions made by larger governments.

Researchers compiling or verifying such a list should consult the city clerk's records, the county elections archive and contemporary newspapers. It is also worth checking whether a mayor served an interrupted term, resigned before the end of a term or was appointed to fill a vacancy, because these details affect how a list should be presented.

For most readers, the list is valuable as a way of understanding the continuity of local government and the people who shaped the city's development. A reliable version will present each name with the years of service, note any gaps or uncertainties in the record, and cite the sources used to establish the dates. Readers who need precise information for research or legal purposes should confirm each entry against the official records.

The Fontainebleau Forest is a large woodland region about 60 kilometres southeast of Paris, known for its sandstone outcrops, its marked trails and its long association with royal hunting. The forest covers a substantial area of mostly broadleaved and mixed woodland, and it has been protected and managed for centuries as part of the royal estate around the palace of Fontainebleau.

A tour of the forest usually follows a combination of marked paths, rocky ridges and open clearings, where visitors can see the distinctive sandstone formations that shape the landscape. The rocks, which were formed from ancient sand deposits, appear in a variety of shapes, some rounded, some flat-topped, and many sit in clusters among the trees. Their surfaces and textures have made the area famous among climbers, who come to test their skills on boulders of varying height and difficulty.

Routes through the forest have been developed over many years, and the network of paths is maintained by public agencies and by volunteer groups. Trail markers, information boards and signposts help visitors plan their route, and some areas are reserved for particular activities so that wildlife and the forest's ecosystems are protected. Visitors are asked to follow the marked routes and to avoid damaging the vegetation or the rock surfaces.

Historically, the forest was a hunting ground for French kings, and its roads and clearings were laid out to suit the royal hunt. Many of the forest's tracks still reflect that history, and visitors can often find traces of old boundaries, stone markers and carriage routes that were used by the court. The palace of Fontainebleau, with its gardens and galleries, is a major attraction in its own right and is often visited together with the forest.

Ecologically, the forest supports a range of plant and animal species that depend on its mix of woodland, heath and sandy ground. Some of the plants found on the rock faces are adapted to dry, nutrient-poor conditions, and the forest's habitats are monitored for changes caused by visitor pressure, climate and disease. Conservation measures aim to balance public access with the protection of the environment.

Anyone planning a tour should check the current access rules, the weather and the condition of the trails before setting out, because some routes may be closed for maintenance or for the protection of nesting birds and other wildlife. Maps and guides published by local tourism offices provide details of the most popular routes, and they often include advice on suitable footwear and safety.

Fouquieria diguetii is a species of flowering plant in the family Fouquieriaceae, a small group of shrubs and trees native to the arid regions of Mexico and the south-western United States. The plant belongs to a genus that is best known through the ocotillo, whose long, thin, spine-covered stems are a distinctive feature of many desert landscapes.

The species is native to western Mexico, where it grows in dry scrub and rocky slopes, often in areas that receive little rain for much of the year. Like other members of its genus, it has a mostly leafless growth habit for much of the time, with its small leaves appearing mainly after rain and then falling as conditions dry out again. This strategy allows the plant to conserve water during long dry spells.

The stems are typically thin and branching, arising from a base that may be woody and partially buried in the ground. Many fouquierias have stems that bear spines or thorns, which discourage herbivores and reduce water loss. The flowers are usually produced in clusters at the tips of the branches, and they are often brightly coloured, attracting hummingbirds and insects that help with pollination.

Taxonomists have worked to clarify the relationships between the species of Fouquieria, in part because the plants can vary considerably with local conditions and their appearance can differ between populations. Morphological features such as the shape of the flowers, the arrangement of the leaves and the form of the stems are used to distinguish one species from another, and some names have been revised as more information has become available.

In the wild, the plant plays an ecological role in the community where it grows, providing shelter and food for a range of animals. Its flowers are visited by pollinators, and the dense spiny stems can offer nesting or resting places for small birds and reptiles. Changes in land use, grazing and climate can all affect its populations, and conservation assessments take account of these pressures.

Fouquieria species have also attracted interest from gardeners and horticulturists, who value their striking form and their tolerance of dry conditions. Cultivation outside the native range requires attention to drainage and to the timing of watering, since the plants are adapted to long periods without moisture and can suffer from overwatering.

Readers seeking detailed botanical information should consult a regional flora or a recognised herbarium record, because descriptions of species in this group can change as new studies appear. Distribution maps, specimen records and taxonomic revisions provide the most reliable basis for any statement about where the species occurs and how it is classified.

After a review of hundreds of thousands of emails, the FBI has once again cleared Hillary Clinton over her use of a private email server while she was secretary of state. The decision brings to a close a second look at the matter, which had been reopened only weeks before a presidential election and had dominated much of the campaign's final stretch.

The private server had been set up for Clinton's use at her family home in New York, and its existence became one of the most debated aspects of her time at the State Department. Several investigations and congressional inquiries had examined the server before the latest announcement. Clinton has acknowledged that using a private server was a mistake, but she has rejected the claim that she intentionally mishandled classified information.

The bureau's latest review focused on messages found on a computer that had been seized in a separate investigation. The agency said it had examined the material to determine whether it changed its earlier conclusions. Officials said the new review did not alter the findings made in July, when the FBI recommended that no criminal charges be brought against Clinton. The announcement was made in a letter to congressional committees that had asked for information on the matter.

Clinton's campaign welcomed the decision and argued that the investigation had been a distraction from the issues that mattered to voters. Supporters said the outcome confirmed their view that the case had been overstated, while critics said the timing of the announcement raised questions about the bureau's judgment.

The case has been one of the most contested episodes of the election, and the handling of the investigation by the FBI director has been widely debated in the press and among politicians. Some commentators argued that the agency's public statements had gone further than normal practice would suggest, while others said the director had acted to keep Congress informed.

The original inquiry examined whether classified information had been mishandled through the use of a private server during Clinton's time at the State Department. Investigators reviewed large numbers of messages, including some that had been deleted and later recovered, and their findings were central to the debate about the candidate's suitability for office.

Legal experts noted that the threshold for criminal charges in cases of this kind is high, and that prosecutors generally require evidence of intent as well as of careless handling. Whether the matter will be raised again is unclear, but the episode has left a lasting mark on the election and on public trust in the agencies involved.

Election analysts said the episode had shaped the final weeks of the campaign in ways that were difficult to measure, since it dominated coverage and shifted the attention of voters and the media. Reporters continued to examine how the decision had been reached and what it revealed about the process.

More than a third of footballers surveyed in Scotland say they have received threats from the stands on a match day, according to a players' union. The findings point to a level of abuse that many players say they have come to accept as part of the game.

The union said the abuse ranged from insults and taunts to direct threats of violence, and that some players had felt unable to go to matches without fear for their safety. Some of the threats were directed at players' families and were posted online after matches, which the union said made the problem harder to address. Its representatives said the problem was not confined to any one club or division and that it affected players at every level of the professional game.

Players described the impact on their performance and on their families, with some saying that threats made them reluctant to travel to away fixtures or to take part in community events. Several said that they had reported incidents to their clubs, but that the responses had not always been consistent or clear enough to give them confidence.

Clubs and football authorities have been under pressure to tackle abuse more firmly, and many have introduced codes of conduct, stewarding improvements and reporting systems for fans. Critics say that stronger sanctions are needed, including bans and clearer action against clubs whose supporters repeatedly behave in threatening ways. Several clubs have said they are working to identify repeat offenders, though they add that enforcement depends on evidence and cooperation from stewards and the police.

Police have also been involved in some cases, and officers have said that they will investigate threats made in person or online where there is evidence of a criminal offence. Campaigners argue that the problem can only be solved through cooperation between clubs, police, governing bodies and supporters' organisations, and that the message must be clear that abuse of players is unacceptable.

Supporters' groups have pointed out that most fans behave responsibly and that the actions of a minority should not be used to condemn the wider crowd. They have called for a shared approach that encourages the vast majority of supporters to speak out when they witness abuse, and for education programmes that explain the impact of threats on players and their families.

The players' union said it would continue to press for improvements and to support members who have been targeted. It is expected to share its findings with clubs and with the national governing body in the coming weeks, and it has urged fans to treat players with the same respect they expect for themselves.

Anyone in Poland who uses language implying that the Polish state or nation bore responsibility for Nazi German atrocities could face a prison term or a fine, under rules the conservative government has defended. The measure amends the law governing the country's Institute of National Remembrance and is intended to protect Poland's reputation abroad and to counter what officials describe as false claims about the Second World War.

Supporters of the measure argue that the phrase Polish death camps and similar expressions are misleading, because the camps were built and run by Nazi Germany on occupied Polish territory. They say Poles were also victims of German occupation and that their suffering should be recognised accurately in international discussion.

Critics, including historians and some foreign governments, say the law could chill legitimate research and public debate. They warn that it risks restricting discussion of the role some Poles played in crimes against Jews during the war. Israel and the United States expressed concern while the legislation was being debated, and historians warned that vague wording could allow prosecutors to target scholars and journalists.

The government has defended the measure as a necessary step to correct a pattern of misrepresentation in foreign media and textbooks. Officials argue that the law targets deliberate distortion rather than genuine historical inquiry, and they say academic work will not be affected if it is conducted in good faith. Some European countries have similar laws that penalise the denial of crimes against humanity, and supporters point to those as precedents.

The dispute has deep roots in the history of the Second World War, when Poland was invaded by Germany in 1939 and lost a far larger share of its population than most countries, including most of its Jewish citizens, to occupation and the Holocaust. Many Poles feel that their country's wartime experience is poorly understood abroad, and the debate often touches on sensitive questions of memory and national identity.

Legal experts have pointed out that the bill's wording leaves room for different interpretations, and that the threshold for prosecution could depend on how a court understands the intent of a speaker. They say clearer definitions would reduce uncertainty for researchers, journalists and teachers who work on wartime history.

The row has also affected relations with partners in Europe and beyond, and diplomats have said the measure is likely to come up in future discussions. Whether the law will be enforced, and how often, remains to be seen, but its passage has ensured that questions about wartime memory will stay prominent in Polish public life.

The United States has undergone a striking change in its energy position, one that few observers would have predicted only a few years ago. The country has moved from worry about declining domestic output and dependence on imports to become one of the world's largest producers of oil and natural gas, and its exports have reshaped energy markets in Europe and Asia.

Much of the change has been driven by advances in drilling and hydraulic fracturing, which have made it possible to extract oil and gas from shale formations that were once considered uneconomic. Technology has improved the speed, precision and cost of wells, and producers have learned to recover more resources from each site than they could before.

The rise of shale production has had wide effects. Gas prices fell for a period, encouraging power companies to switch from coal to gas, and petrochemical manufacturers gained access to cheaper feedstock. Liquefied natural gas terminals have been built along the coasts to ship American gas overseas, creating new trade relationships with buyers who had previously depended on a small number of suppliers.

The shift has not been without difficulty. Energy prices have been volatile, and producers have had to cope with boom and bust cycles that can leave companies heavily indebted and communities dependent on a single industry. Environmental groups have raised concerns about methane emissions, water use and the disposal of waste, and regulators have responded with new rules in some states.

Renewable energy has also expanded rapidly, with wind and solar capacity growing in many regions. Analysts say the grid is becoming more complex as different sources of power are added, and that investment in transmission lines, storage and flexible generation will be needed to keep supply reliable as the mix changes.

Policy has played a role too. Tax incentives, research funding and changing regulatory frameworks have all influenced investment decisions, and their effects are debated. Supporters of current arrangements argue that they have helped secure supply and reduce emissions where gas has displaced coal, while critics say the benefits have been uneven and that long-term commitments to cleaner energy have been underfunded.

For households, the effects are felt mainly through electricity and heating bills, which respond to fuel prices and to the cost of building new generation. Consumers have therefore watched shifts in supply with close attention, even when the underlying changes are gradual and hard to see.

Looking ahead, the sector faces several open questions. Demand for fuel in transport and industry is uncertain, global prices depend on decisions made far from American shores, and the pace of technological change could shift the balance between sources quickly. Yet few would deny that the scale of the reversal has been remarkable, and it will remain a central reference point for debates about energy security for years to come.

The 2013 Chattanooga Mocs football team represented the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga during the 2013 college football season. The Mocs played their home games at Finley Stadium in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and competed in the Southern Conference, a league of universities from the southeastern United States that plays at the Football Championship Subdivision level.

Like other programmes in the Football Championship Subdivision, the team operated with a limited number of scholarships and relied on a roster that combined recruited players and walk-ons. The season was organised around a schedule of conference games and non-conference matches, and the team's results in league play shaped its prospects for postseason competition.

Finley Stadium served as the team's home ground for home matches, and attendance depended on the schedule, the weather and the level of competition. Game-day operations were coordinated by university staff, who worked with local services to manage traffic and crowd flow. Away fixtures required long road trips across the region, which affected travel plans for players, staff and supporters alike.

Season summaries for teams of this kind typically cover the record in conference play, the team's performance in key games and any notable individual achievements, such as those recognised by conference or national awards. Coaches and players in the programme were generally expected to balance athletic development with academic progress, as at other universities in the division.

The season is documented in the university's athletics records, conference standings and local press coverage, which together provide the most reliable account of results and statistics. Readers who need specific scores, dates or player statistics should consult these sources, because summaries compiled from memory or from secondary material can contain errors.

Because the Football Championship Subdivision includes many programmes with similar structures and calendars, it is easy to confuse one team's season with another's.
